name: AirPlay 2 Multi-Room
description: Adds an AirPlay 2 player to Kiosk Satellite's Media Player, so the kiosk groups with HomePods and other AirPlay 2 speakers for multi-room audio from an iPhone, iPad or Mac. Pick it under Settings > Media Player > Player. Follows the sender's clock over PTP, which needs Shizuku running as root, and plays through Kiosk Satellite's own output, so Now Playing, lyrics, ducking and the echo canceller all work. Audio only. Not affiliated with Apple.
author: Ian White

settings.title: Speaker name
settings.description: The name shown in the AirPlay menu on your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Leave empty to use this kiosk's device name.

settings.title: Audio offset
settings.description: Shift AirPlay audio later (positive) or earlier (negative), from -3 to +3 seconds in steps of 0.01 s, to line it up with video or other speakers. Type a value, or nudge it with the buttons below. Applies straight away.

settings.title: Start Shizuku as root at boot
settings.description: Optional. Shizuku stops when the kiosk restarts, and multi-room needs it running as root. On, the plugin starts it at boot by signing in to this device's own ADB as root with a key you allow once. Needs Rooted debugging and ADB kept on port 5555 (see the README). Turning it off removes the plugin's key from Android's trusted ADB keys.

settings.title: Port
settings.description: TCP port for AirPlay connections, 1024 to 65535. The default keeps clear of Kiosk Satellite's own AirPlay receiver.

settings.title: AirPlay device ID
settings.description: Empty: made from this device, so every kiosk has its own, Fleet Management included. Only for troubleshooting: an ID set here replaces it, and Fleet Management copies it to every kiosk on the profile.

settings.title: Feature flags
settings.description: For troubleshooting only. Leave empty for the default (0x401FCA00,0x1C340, as shairport-sync advertises). See the README.

settings.title: Shizuku is running as root
settings.description: Set by the plugin to switch the Shizuku button between Start and Started. Changing it here has no effect.

settings.title: ADB key from an earlier version
settings.description: Only versions 0.6.2 to 0.7.0 kept the boot start's ADB key here. The plugin moves it to private storage on this device and clears this setting by itself.

buttons.title: Start Shizuku now
buttons.label: Start
buttons.description: Starts Shizuku as root through this device's ADB, the same way the boot start does. The first time, approve the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt on the kiosk screen with Always allow.

buttons.title: Shizuku is running
buttons.label: Started
buttons.description: Shizuku runs as root. Tap to check that the boot start can still reach ADB as root.
